facts.raw_span: A 34-year-old breastfeeding woman presented with a subacute painful, warm, and nodular skin lesion at the left side of her body localized between the neck and breast, measuring approximately 3 × 4 cm
One year earlier, the patient had visited an East-Turkish region and experienced a similar lesion that disappeared spontaneously after 10 days
She did not report consumption of unpasteurized dairy products or contact with livestock
Born prematurely at 28 weeks' gestation with intracerebral bleeding and left hemiplegia, resulting in hydrocephaly, for which a VP shunt was placed
The VP shunt was completely revised at age 14 due to disconnection
Fourteen years later, a second revision was performed due to intracranial blockage, with a novel VP shunt placed at the right side of the thorax
No systemic or other localized symptoms present
Heart rate: 89 beats/min
Blood pressure: 124/73 mm Hg
Body temperature: 36.3 °C
Leukocyte count: 11.15 × 10⁹/L
Culture: positive for B. melitensis biovar 3
